title: Compatibility safety net strategies for private control plane upgrades
body:
Purpose
This is a working runbook that collects strategies, lightweight tooling patterns, and Terraform notes intended to provide a compatibility safety net during control-plane upgrades for Private deployments (VPC / on-prem). The focus here is minimizing customer-visible API changes, preserving in-flight state, and keeping quick rollback paths. This is intentionally operational and engineer-facing — not a marketing doc.

Scope and constraints
- Applies to Private control plane upgrades (components: control-plane API, placement/orchestration, runtime agent handshake).
- Excludes heavy data-model migrations that require DB downtime (those should be handled via dedicated migration jobs).
- Assumes customer VPCs may have restricted egress and that artifact distribution might be via signed bundles (airgap).

Goals
- No more than 10s of added tail-latency during normal traffic after cutover.
- No customer API contract-breaking without an opt-in migration window.
- Clear automated rollback triggers based on SLO regressions and error budgets.
- Maintain ability to serve older runtime versions by introducing compatibility adapters rather than hard-cutting clients.

High-level approach (safety-net tiers)
1) API negotiation / header-based versioning shim (non-invasive):
   - Deploy a small gateway-side adapter that inspects X-Redwood-Client-Version (or similar) and rewrites/augments requests for older agents.
   - Adapter resides in control-plane edge; cheap and reversible.
   - Use for small contract changes: renamed fields, swapped enum values, optional params.

2) Runtime feature flags + dual-protocol acceptance: 
   - Introduce feature-gated endpoints on control plane that accept both V1 and V2 payload shapes; gate with tenant-level flags.
   - Default to V1 behavior unless tenant explicitly opts in.

3) Proxy-level KV cache mirroring / warmup: 
   - Before cutting over, run background jobs that pre-populate runtime KV caches with expected model prefixes to avoid cold-start regression spikes.
   - For private deployments, provide an offline warmup bundle (tar.gz) customers can load into local cache priming job.

4) Canary-by-tenant + traffic shaping: 
   - Ship control-plane new release to small tenant slices first (use tenant labels).
   - Gradually ramp producers of high-throughput traffic later.

Preflight checklist (quick)
- [ ] Verify Terraform plan against known state (capture plan output to artifact).
- [ ] Confirm artifact signing and offline delivery path for airgapped customers.
- [ ] Run compatibility tests: api-contract smoke, runtime handshake, kv-warmup simulation.
- [ ] Backup control-plane DB snapshot and export critical config keys.
- [ ] Validate observability (traces, metrics, logs) ingestion for new binaries.

Operational probes (what to watch)
- Error increase: 5xx rate > baseline + 2x in any 5m window => immediate throttle/rollback evaluation.
- Latency: p95 > baseline + 30% for 10m => investigate batching/queueing regressions.
- Cache-miss surge: sustained cache miss delta > 5x baseline for 15m => trigger KV warmup and consider rollback.
- Authentication failures: any uptick in auth/token errors for control-plane agent registrations -> block progressive rollout.

Rollback triggers and automated rollback plan
- Triggers (any 2 of the following within 20m):
  * p95 latency spike above threshold,
  * 5xx error-rate doubling,
  * >10% reduction in throughput for top-10 tenants,
  * Breakage of agent handshake (registration failure rate >1%).
- Automated actions:
  1) Route new-tier traffic back to previous control-plane instances (routing flag flip).
  2) Scale down new control-plane replicas gracefully (drain connections with 30s grace).
  3) Re-apply previous Terraform state via saved plan (see notes below).
  4) If DB migrations executed, run explicit backout scripts (these must be vetted preflight).

Terraform module notes (practical)
- Module version pinning: always pin control-plane module versions in tenant manifests. Keep module changelog entry for every exported var that affects public API.
- Immutable artifacts: store signed artifact id and checksum as a variable; do not rely on 'latest' image tags.
- State locks: require manual approval step to unlock state in airgapped or high-risk tenants.
- Plan capture: store terraform plan output in S3/MinIO and tag with upgrade run id. This becomes the canonical rollback plan.
- Minimal diff approach: expose 'feature_toggle' variables per tenant to apply compatibility flags without code deploys.

API compatibility design patterns (concrete)
- Additive-only approach for fields: prefer adding optional fields with defaults parsed by both old and new agents.
- Deprecation window: advertise deprecations for at least 90 days; allow opt-in to new behavior during that time.
- Version negotiation header example: X-RW-API-Version: "1.3". Gate breaking transforms behind adapter that checks this header.
- Operational escape hatch: X-RW-Compatibility=legacy to force legacy handling for specific requests.

KV/state migration strategy (non-disruptive technique)
- Shadow-migrate: write dual-writers for new branch but keep reads from legacy until canary shows parity.
- Reconciliation job: compare digest counts and top-k keys between old and new stores; fail cutover if >0.1% divergence on hot keyset.
- Cold-start mitigation: provide a bulk-snapshot restore operation that can hydrate runtime caches from control-plane export.

Telemetry preservation and trace continuity
- Maintain trace-id pass-through between runtime and control-plane. If header name changes, introduce adapter that maps old->new ids.
- Preserve search tags and tenant ids to keep historical dashboards functional.
- Backfill strategy: if a short telemetry gap occurs, run a focused backfill using retained logs and export to observability tenant workspace.

Airgapped / offline customer considerations
- Deliver signed bundle with both old and new control-plane binaries + migration scripts.
- Provide 'upgrade lab' script that can be executed by customer SRE with automatic preflight checks and dry-run.
- Ensure KMS/HSM key rotation plan is included; avoid automatic rotation during cutover window.

Runbook: step-by-step (0 -> full cutover)
0) PREP: gather plan id, backup ids, owner pager, and Slack channel.
1) DRY-RUN: apply module with feature_toggle only (no binary update). Run smoke tests.
2) CANARY-1: deploy control-plane nodes with new binary to canary pool (tenant labels small). Monitor 30m.
3) CANARY-2: widen to medium pool; enable KV warmup jobs for medium tenants. Monitor 1h.
4) ROLL: ramp to 50% by request-weighted routing. Keep legacy adapter enabled.
5) OBSERVE: collect metrics/traces and run automated parity checks.
6) COMPLETION: flip feature_toggle to default=true for a second, then deprecate adapter after 90 days.

Quick incident notes (what to do if things go wrong)
- If agent registrations fail: flip routing to legacy control-plane and contact infra team to pause rollout.
- If DB schema mismatch detected: stop new control-plane writes immediately and run reconciliation; notify platform DB team.
- For irreversible migration steps discovered in-flight: escalate to the upgrade owner and run postmortem to avoid repeat.

Open TODOs / follow-ups
- Build a lightweight adapter prototype (node/Go) that can run in the edge and hold shims for at least five typical field transforms. Owner: Daniel.
- Add terraform plan capture hook into our CI pipeline and store per-run artifacts for 180 days. Owner: Aisha.
- Define exact SLO thresholds per tenant size class for automated rollback logic. Owner: Priya.

References and example commands
- Capture terraform plan: terraform plan -out=plan.binary && terraform show -json plan.binary > plan.json && upload-to-artifact-store plan.json
- KV warmup job (example): python tools/kv_warmup.py --bundle kv-snapshot.tgz --target runtime://10.0.5.3:9000 --concurrency 8
- Rollback apply (safe): terraform apply -input=false -auto-approve saved/plan-id-1234.tfplan

Post-cutover checklist (24h)
- [ ] Confirm per-tenant error rate within historical baseline.
- [ ] Validate that 100% of canary tenants have no handshake regressions.
- [ ] Sweep audit logs for any auth/key anomalies.
- [ ] Schedule adapter sunsetting and communication plan if no issues after 90 days.

Appendix: quick compatibility shim examples
- Field rename shim pseudocode: if missing(request.new_field) and request.old_field: request.new_field = transform(request.old_field)
- Header rewrite: if header X-RW-API-Version absent -> set to 1.0 (legacy)

This is a draft — please add observations from dry-runs, canary metrics, and any edge-case failures encountered. Keep notes below as plaintext samples of incident timelines for the postmortem.
